reviews.reviewer: Reviewer A — F-D3-01 closure audit (applyEdit/editTarget split, GeoARSessionManager.swift)

closures.item: (a) F-D3-01 core: "Place on ground" mutates, persists, and clears/sets groundLockBaseY coherently
closures.proof: GeoARSessionManager.swift:2186 now calls `applyEdit(to: drop.id, height: <clamped>, commit: true)` directly instead of the gesture entry point (round-3 baseline `git show 91216b7:...` :2123 called `adjustNearestDrop`, which returned at its `guard gestureHeld` with heldGestures==0 on a button tap). The mutation chain is now reached: heightAboveGround set :2038, placedDrops[id] written :2041, holder.position.y += Float(height-oldHeight) :2051 (delta = groundY+0.005-base.y, so the holder lands exactly on the measured surface), grounding disc re-seated :2053, and — since commit==true and the drop is neither a roomDrop (:2078) nor a demoDrop (:2080) — `library.update(edited, persist: true)` fires at :2084/:2090, so the snap survives relaunch and reaches Firestore. Lock ordering is coherent and synchronous on @MainActor (class is @MainActor, :25): applyEdit's commit tail nils the old lock at :2100-2102 (`height != nil` ⇒ manual-override clear), then the caller writes the new lock at :2188. That lock is then honoured by both consumers — the geo tick (`let y = groundLockBaseY[drop.id] ?? ...` :1845-1846) and applyVPSTransform (:962-963) — both of which force y to exactly groundY+0.005, the same y applyEdit put the holder at. The round-3 harm chain (tap-does-nothing → orphaned lock drags the drop later → reverts on relaunch) is dead at every link. HUD readout also updates: applyEdit sets `nearestDrop = drop` (:2043, the `nearestDrop?.id == id` disjunct holds because snap resolved its target FROM nearestDrop at :2132), so ARScreen.swift:572's `syncSliders()` immediately after the button call reads the new height at ARScreen.swift:606 — FT-40(b) is mechanically satisfied.

closures.item: (a) no-surface decline routed to the NON-critical banner slot
closures.proof: GeoARSessionManager.swift:2169-2178: `guard let groundY else { showPersistError("Couldn't find the ground here — move closer and try again", critical: false); return }`. showPersistError at :93-106 refuses to overwrite a visible critical message when called non-critically (`if !critical, persistErrorText != nil, persistErrorIsCritical { return }`, :94-96), so a declined convenience snap can never evict a data-loss toast. The `return` at :2177 precedes the groundLockBaseY write at :2188, so a declined snap leaves no orphaned lock. Unchanged by round 4 and still intact.

closures.item: (b)(i) adjustNearestDrop binding — live slider drag on a captured drop
closures.proof: ARScreen.swift:504/531/558 call beginLiveEdit on the editing-began edge; GeoARSessionManager.swift:451-455 increments heldGestures and captures `editingDropID = nearestDrop?.id`. Each drag tick (ARScreen.swift:494/521/548) enters at :2005 with capture non-nil, so `editTarget` returns the capture (:511 `if let capture { return capture }`) — never nearest. The freeze holds while the capture lives (updateNearest returns early at :1655 `guard editingDropID == nil`), so nearest cannot move under the finger. lastLiveEditTickAt is refreshed on non-commit ticks only (:2010), which is what keeps the 1.5 s/30 s abandonment clock (:472-477) honest.

closures.item: (b)(ii) programmatic authored edit
closures.proof: The only two authored callers bypass the gesture entry point entirely: snapNearestDropToGround → applyEdit (:2186) and relocateNearestDrop, which has always carried its own mutation body (:2220-2290). `applyEdit` is private (:2022) and has exactly two call sites (grep: :2016, :2186). ARScreen has no other manager edit call (ARScreen.swift:494/506/521/533/548/560 are the six slider callbacks, :571 the snap button, :621 relocate). So no non-gesture caller can be refused by the gesture gate any more. Caveat recorded as F-D4-02: the `authored:` parameter of editTarget is passed a literal nil at its one call site (:2007), so the authored branch (:510) is dead code in production.

closures.item: (b)(iii) held-gesture re-bind refusal — is the STATE-L1 wrong-drop persist still dead?
closures.proof: The single-gesture refusal is intact: a tick with no capture and no finger down returns nil at :512 (`return held ? nearest : nil`) and adjustNearestDrop returns at :2008 — identical semantics to round 3 (`git show 91216b7:...` :1963-1966). removePerDropState now also zeroes the counter when the captured target dies (:1629-1633), so a finger over a deleted drop cannot re-bind. BUT the refusal is bypassed for a SECOND concurrent gesture: applyEdit's commit tail clears the shared capture unconditionally (:2099) while heldGestures can still be > 0, leaving the state (capture: nil, held: true) in which editTarget deliberately binds to the now-UNFROZEN nearest (:1655 passes once editingDropID is nil). See F-D4-01 — round 4's counter converts round 3's safe failure mode (second slider goes dead) into a wrong-drop live edit and persist.

closures.item: (c) applyEdit STATE-4 strict resolve + vanish guard
closures.proof: :2030-2035 resolves strictly from owned state (`placedDrops[id] ?? roomDrops[id] ?? demoDrops.first`) with no nearestDrop fallback, exactly as round 2 left it; the failure arm now guards its clear (`if editingDropID == id`, :2032) so an authored miss cannot clear another gesture's capture. Removal ordering is safe: removePerDropState nils placedDrops[id] (:1620) and clears the capture/counter (:1629-1633) before any later tick can resolve, and room drops are only destroyed through clearRoomDrops (:695-704) which routes every id through the same helper. No path was found where a gesture tick lands on a drop already removed from all three maps.

closures.item: (c) nearestDrop clobber guard
closures.proof: :2043 `if nearestDrop == nil || nearestDrop?.id == id { nearestDrop = drop }` — an authored edit of a non-nearest target no longer overwrites the HUD's nearest (round-3 baseline wrote `nearestDrop = drop` unconditionally, `git show 91216b7:...` :1985). Both current authored callers target nearestDrop itself, so the guard is defensive today; the `nearestDrop == nil` disjunct has a cosmetic residual (nearestDrop set with nearestDropDistance still nil, ARScreen.swift:294-295 hides the title/distance line until the freeze lifts) — recorded in residuals.

closures.item: (c) commit tail clearing editingDropID — any path where an edit lands on a removed/replaced drop mid-gesture?
closures.proof: The split is incomplete: the gesture bookkeeping stayed inside the MUTATION half. :2099 (`if editingDropID == id { editingDropID = nil }`) and :2098 (`liveEditingDrops.remove(id)`) run on the authored path too, contradicting applyEdit's own doc comment at :2019-2021 ("programmatic (authored) callers commit to an explicit target with no gesture state read or written"). Concretely: a "Place on ground" tap while a thumb rests on the height slider (same panel, ARScreen.swift:569-579 sits directly under the three sliders) resolves the same id as the capture, clears editingDropID at :2099, releases the nearest freeze at :1655 AND drops the VPS "never fight the finger" guard at :952 — all while the finger is still down. The edit does not land on a removed drop, but the NEXT tick of that live gesture can land on a different drop. See F-D4-01.

closures.item: (d) Round4BindingTests pin the caller's binding (the round-3 caller-context lesson)
closures.proof: Zero tests construct the manager: `grep -rn 'GeoARSessionManager(' AugmentMeRealityTests/` returns nothing, and the only manager references in the whole target are the five static `GeoARSessionManager.editTarget(` calls at WaveDTests.swift:468/473/479/484/489. The pure table therefore pins editTarget's body and nothing about the call site. Revert the actual fix — re-point snapNearestDropToGround at adjustNearestDrop (:2186 → the round-3 line) — and all five rows still pass, i.e. the suite stays 146/146 with the CRITICAL fully reintroduced. Worse, the only two rows that distinguish round 4 from round 3 are the two `authored:` rows (:466-476), and `authored` is a literal nil at the one production call site (:2007), so those rows guard parameter space that cannot execute. FT-40 (FIELDTESTS.md:234-238) is currently the ONLY thing standing between this CRITICAL and a regression, and it is a manual field assertion, not a gate. See F-D4-02.

findings.claim: applyEdit's commit tail clears the SHARED gesture capture (`editingDropID`) regardless of whether other fingers are still down and regardless of whether the caller is the authored path — so a commit on one slider (or a "Place on ground" tap) strands a still-live drag in the (capture: nil, held: true) state, which editTarget deliberately binds to the now-unfrozen `nearestDrop`. Round 4's heldGestures counter is what makes this reachable: in round 3 `gestureHeld = false` on commit made the surviving drag's ticks REFUSED (dead slider, safe); now heldGestures stays > 0, so those ticks are ACCEPTED and re-bind. The counter added for F-D3-04 upgraded a benign failure into the exact wrong-drop persist STATE-L1 exists to kill.
findings.harm: Two-finger sequence in the adjust panel (three sliders stacked at ARScreen.swift:486-566 with the snap button at :569 directly beneath them): thumb on the scale slider, index finger releases the height slider. adjustNearestDrop(:2011-2014) decrements heldGestures 2→1, applyEdit's tail nils editingDropID (:2099), and updateNearest's freeze (:1655 `guard editingDropID == nil`) lifts on the very next 400 ms tick (:1107). The user pans a few degrees, nearest flips from A to N (:1677 for geo drops, :1660-1667 for room drops, which are AR-distance-sensitive and flip on a step). The still-live scale drag's next tick binds to N (:2007/:512), mutates placedDrops[N] with a value seeded from A by syncSliders (ARScreen.swift:607), pushes it into the live library (:2090, persist:false), and on release persists it — `library.update(persist: true)` at :2084/:2090 — writing another user's/another drop's size or rotation to disk AND Firestore, visible to every viewer, with no undo. Collateral on the same trigger: SWE-5's anti-jump property is lost (the nearest change fires ARScreen.swift:601 `onChange(of: nearestDrop?.id) { syncSliders() }`, so the thumb jumps mid-drag), applyVPSTransform's "never fight the finger" guard is dropped early (:952, via `liveEditingDrops.remove(id)` at :2098), and if the new nearest resolves to nil the whole adjustPanel disappears from under the finger (ARScreen.swift:289). Same defect via one finger + one tap: "Place on ground" tapped while a slider is held resolves the captured drop, and :2099 clears the capture even though applyEdit's doc comment at :2019-2021 promises the authored path writes no gesture state.
findings.fix: Finish the split the round was named for: take ALL gesture bookkeeping out of the mutation half. In applyEdit delete the `editingDropID` writes at :2032 and :2099 (keep `liveEditingDrops` insert/remove, which is per-drop render state, or move it too), and do the tail in adjustNearestDrop after the delegate call — `if commit, editingDropID == id, heldGestures == 0 { editingDropID = nil }`. Because the decrement already happens at :2014 before the call, the single-slider case still clears exactly as today, while a second held gesture keeps the capture (and the freeze) until the LAST finger lifts — which is the correct semantics for three sliders that were all seeded from the same nearest drop. On the failure arm, replace :2032 with the same caller-side handling. ~6 lines, no behaviour change to any single-gesture path.
findings.test_case: The manager is untestable today (no test constructs it; placedDrops/editingDropID are private), so the seam is the fix: extract the gesture state machine as a value type — `struct GestureBinding { var capture: UUID?; var held: Int; mutating func begin(nearest: UUID?); mutating func tick(nearest: UUID?) -> UUID?; mutating func commit(nearest: UUID?) -> UUID?; mutating func authoredCommit(_ id: UUID); mutating func targetRemoved(_ id: UUID) }` — and drive it with the EXACT ARScreen callback sequence rather than literal states: begin(nearest: A) [height], begin(nearest: A) [scale], commit(nearest: A) [height release], then tick(nearest: N) with a DIFFERENT nearest, and assert the returned target is still A, not N; a second case runs authoredCommit(A) between begin and tick and asserts the same. Both cases fail on today's code (they return N). Pair with a field case FT-41: two thumbs, release one slider, pan until the HUD's nearest title changes, release the second — assert on relaunch that only the intended drop changed.

findings.claim: Round4BindingTests' editTarget table is vacuous with respect to the CRITICAL it was written to guard. Three of the five rows (capture-wins :477-482, unheld-refusal :483-486, held→nearest :487-492) assert behaviour the round-3 code already had — `git show 91216b7:AugmentMeReality/AR/GeoARSessionManager.swift` :1962-1966 is capture-else-held-else-refuse, identical semantics — so they cannot distinguish round 4 from round 3. The only two rows that could (the `authored:` rows, :466-476) exercise a parameter that no call site ever populates: the single caller passes the literal `authored: nil` (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2007), because the authored path was routed AROUND editTarget (:2186 calls applyEdit directly) rather than THROUGH it. Net: zero rows fail if the fix is reverted.
findings.harm: The suite stays 146/146 green with "Place on ground" a silent no-op again — precisely the failure mode the counsel named as round 3's lesson ("the suite is green with a dead flagship button because no test constructs the manager"). A future refactor that re-unifies the two entry points, or any change that reintroduces a gesture-state read on the authored path, ships undetected; the only detector is FT-40, a manual field assertion added in the same commit (FIELDTESTS.md:234-238), which does not run in CI and cannot gate a merge. This is the round-3 defect repeating one level up: correct pure functions asserted against state the caller never produces.
findings.fix: Make the parameter load-bearing so the table pins the caller: have snapNearestDropToGround resolve through the same predicate — `guard let id = Self.editTarget(capture: editingDropID, held: gestureHeld, authored: drop.id, nearest: nearestDrop?.id) else { return }` then `applyEdit(to: id, ...)`. Behaviour is identical (authored wins at :510) but the authored rows now guard live code, and re-routing snap through the gesture gate would flip the first row. Alternatively, if the intent is that authored edits never touch editTarget, delete the `authored` parameter and the two rows rather than keep decorative coverage. Either way, add the value-type seam from F-D4-01 so at least one test drives the caller's SEQUENCE.
findings.test_case: Sequence-driven, not literal-fed: a `PlacementBindingTests` case that replays the ARScreen button handler's steps against the extracted binding/state seam — `authoredCommit(dropID)` with held == 0 and capture == nil must return the dropID (not nil), and the same call with held == 1 and a DIFFERENT capture must still return the dropID while leaving the capture intact. Both assertions trip on the round-3 code (refusal) and on any regression that re-routes the authored path through the gesture gate; neither can be satisfied by a pure table that production never calls with a non-nil authored.

residuals: Clamp-vs-lock divergence, now live for the first time: snapNearestDropToGround clamps the target height to [-2, 20] (:2186) but writes groundLockBaseY unconditionally (:2188). If the correction saturates the band, the local holder is pinned to the measured ground (:1845-1846, :962-963) while the persisted heightAboveGround says something else, so other viewers render the drop up to the clamp error away. Can wait: identical arithmetic to round 3 (only dormant there because the whole call was a no-op), and it needs a drop already >20 m above or >2 m below the surface under it.

`nearestDrop == nil` disjunct at :2043 can set nearestDrop while nearestDropDistance stays nil (removePerDropState nils both at :1642-1643 for a DIFFERENT drop while the capture freezes updateNearest). ARScreen.swift:294-295 then hides the title/distance line for the rest of the drag, and :601 fires a mid-drag syncSliders. Cosmetic, and the freeze lifts on commit.

A refused commit does not decrement heldGestures — the decrement at :2011-2015 sits below the guard at :2005-2008. Unreachable in practice (refusal-while-held requires nearest == nil, which hides the whole panel at ARScreen.swift:289) and the now-ungated 30 s backstop at :1181-1186 clears any latch. Documented, no action.

The 30 s held-gesture backstop (:476) fires on a genuinely stationary finger; if the user then resumes dragging, every remaining tick is refused (correctly, not misbound) and the slider silently stops responding until release. Designed tradeoff from round 3; worth one line in FIELDTESTS rather than code.

STATE-4 resolve window: a remotely deleted drop stays in placedDrops until the next 400 ms prune (:1898/:2437), so a commit inside that window still resurrects it via library.update. Pre-existing since round 2, unchanged by round 4, and bounded by one tick.

No field case covers the two-thumb slider interaction that F-D4-01 turns on — FT-40 (FIELDTESTS.md:234-238) covers ground-snap only. Add FT-41 when F-D4-01 lands so the fix has field evidence, not just a unit assertion.

test_vacuity.reason: This IS round 3's behaviour (91216b7:...:1963 `guard gestureHeld else { return }`). Passes against the code that shipped the CRITICAL.

test_vacuity.reason: The only rows whose behaviour is new in round 4, but the `authored` parameter is a literal nil at the sole call site (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2007) — the real authored path bypasses editTarget entirely (:2186 → applyEdit). Revert :2186 to `adjustNearestDrop(...)` and "Place on ground" is a silent no-op again while all five rows still pass and the suite stays 146/146. Vacuous with respect to the defect it names.

Non-vacuous against PLAN DRIFT: it would trip (`diverged at supports=… recent=…`) if perceptionPlan's reconstruction expression at GeoARSessionManager.swift:1374-1379 were edited away from reconstructionDesired. But it is vacuous against F-D3-02 itself — the defect was caller state, and the resume site's own argument expression (`cameraVisible || Self.cameraRecentlyVisible(now:lastVisible:)`, :566-573) is never evaluated by any test. Same disease as the editTarget table; flagged here because the test lives in my (d) class, and it is another reviewer's item to rule on.

`XCTAssertGreaterThanOrEqual(observedActive, 0)` is a tautology — it cannot fail for any implementation. Its value is entirely as a TSan exerciser under the RSCH-1 leg-1 substitute (DECISIONS.md, RSCH-1 amendment), which the test's own comment concedes. As an XCTest assertion it guards nothing; outside my lane, noted for the record.

reviews.ship_opinion: Round 4 genuinely closes the user-visible CRITICAL: "Place on ground" now mutates the holder, updates placedDrops, persists with `persist: true`, refreshes the HUD readout for syncSliders, and sets the ground lock in the right order after applyEdit's manual-override clear — every link in the round-3 harm chain (tap-does-nothing → moves-by-itself → reverts-on-relaunch) is broken at a traceable line, and the no-surface decline is still routed to the non-critical banner slot. But the split is half-done and the guards are vacuous, so I cannot call round 4 close-able as it stands. The gesture bookkeeping stayed inside the mutation half (:2032, :2099), which means a commit on one slider — or the snap button itself — strands a still-live drag with no capture and a non-zero held counter, the one state in which editTarget binds to an unfrozen nearest; round 4's own heldGestures counter is what turns that from round 3's harmless dead slider into a wrong-drop write to disk and Firestore, i.e. the wave has spent three rounds killing this exact harm and this round moved it rather than removed it. Fix is ~6 lines (F-D4-01) and touches no single-gesture path. Separately, nothing in CI can detect a regression of the CRITICAL: five table rows, three of which round-3 code already satisfies and two of which exercise a parameter that is a literal nil at the only call site — the round-3 caller-context lesson is stated in DECISIONS.md but not yet paid for in the test target. My recommendation: land F-D4-01 and make the table load-bearing (F-D4-02) as a spot fix, then open the field-run gate with FT-40 plus a new two-thumb FT-41; the residuals (clamp-vs-lock, nil-nearest cosmetics, the 30 s backstop tradeoff) are all field-observable and none of them should hold the gate.

reviews.reviewer: Reviewer B — F-D3-02 closure audit (restorer reordering + shared reconstruction predicate)

closures.item: (a) F-D3-02 restorer reorder — cameraDidAppear: is the resume visibility term now TRUE?
closures.proof: ARSessionHolder.swift:61-70 — `manager.markCameraVisible()` at :68 now precedes `startIfNeeded()` at :69. Both are @MainActor and the block is fully synchronous (no await between), so GeoARSessionManager.markCameraVisible (:613-622) sets `cameraVisible = true` (:614) before startIfNeeded's `else if !sessionRunning { manager.resumeSession() }` at ARSessionHolder.swift:109-111. resumeSession reads `cameraVisible` at GeoARSessionManager.swift:573 as the first disjunct of the reconstruction argument — now TRUE. Walked the exact round-3 failure sequence: hide at t=0 (markCameraHidden :598-609 stamps lastCameraVisibleAt), pause fires at t=5 (suspendSession :423-444 zeroes appliedPerception at :438 and sets cameraVisible=false at :426, sessionRunning=false at ARSessionHolder.swift:130), show at t=5.1 → resumePlan.reconstruction = supports && true && pedestrian && !critical = TRUE (:571-577), appliedPerception = that tuple (:581), one session.run (:582). First tick then computes the identical value via perceptionPlan (:1242-1259 → :1374-1379) and setPerception's `guard desired != appliedPerception` (:884) short-circuits — exactly ONE run. Pre-fix this resumed with reconstruction=false and the first tick fired run #2.

closures.item: (a) F-D3-02 restorer reorder — appDidBecomeActive: is the resume visibility term now TRUE?
closures.proof: ARSessionHolder.swift:91-97 — markCameraVisible at :95 precedes startIfNeeded at :96. Reachability walked from the real driver: AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:36-52 fires .background → appDidEnterBackground (:78-81) → suspend() → suspendSession clears manager.cameraVisible (:426) and sessionRunning=false; then .active → configure (:41) → warmWithoutCamera (:44) → appDidBecomeActive (:47). The guard at ARSessionHolder.swift:92 (`cameraVisible, !sessionRunning`) reads the HOLDER's flag, which suspendSession never touches, so it passes; markCameraVisible then makes the manager's flag true before resumeSession reads it at GeoARSessionManager.swift:573. Note the guard can only pass when `attached` is already true (holder.cameraVisible is set only in cameraDidAppear, which itself attaches), so this path always takes the resume branch, never attach.

closures.item: (a) Remaining paths where the ordering could still invert — beginRevealWarmup and attach-first-run
closures.proof: attach-first-run: NO inversion. On the first cameraDidAppear `attached==false`, so startIfNeeded takes the attach branch (ARSessionHolder.swift:105-108); resumeSession is never reached and the visibility term is irrelevant. I checked what the manager does with a visibility mark before attach: markCameraVisible (:613-622) writes only cameraVisible, cameraVisibleAt and timeToFirstObjectMs; attach (:323-328) then overwrites timeToFirstObjectMs=nil, and on a first attach placedHolders is empty so markCameraVisible had already set nil — no divergence. recordTTFOIfNeeded (:2307-2313) uses `cameraVisibleAt ?? attachedAt`, and cameraVisibleAt is now stamped microseconds earlier, which is the more honest reference, not a regression. decideModeAndRun/runGPSCompass (:710-723, :845-875) read no visibility state. `detach()` has zero callers repo-wide, so `attached` is a one-way latch and re-attach cannot happen. beginRevealWarmup (ARSessionHolder.swift:55-59, callers ReceiveScreen.swift:50 and OnboardingView.swift:154): it deliberately does NOT mark visible (the camera surface is off-screen — correct), so the resume relies wholly on the `|| Self.cameraRecentlyVisible(...)` fallback at :574. That fallback is TRUE for exactly the 1.0 s tail between the pause firing (t = pauseGraceSeconds = 5.0, AppConfig.swift:150) and the grace release at t = 6.0 (:487) — so a warmup resume landing in that sliver requests LiDAR mesh with the camera provably hidden and the governor sheds it one to two ticks later. See F-D4-02. Strictly better than round 3 (which double-ran in the same sliver in the opposite direction), but the comment at :566-569 claiming 'one session.run … including on the beginRevealWarmup path inside the grace window' is not true for the tail.

closures.item: (b) BOTH perceptionPlan and resumePlan call the shared reconstructionDesired predicate
closures.proof: The predicate is defined at GeoARSessionManager.swift:494-502. Call site 1 (resume plan): :571-577, inside resumeSession. Call site 2 (tick plan): :1374-1379, inside the nonisolated static perceptionPlan. Grep for `reconstructionDesired` across the app target returns exactly those two call sites plus the definition — there is no third inline copy of the formula left. The two now differ only in how they compose the `cameraRecentlyVisible` ARGUMENT: resumeSession passes `cameraVisible || Self.cameraRecentlyVisible(now:lastVisible:)` (:573-574) while updatePowerTier passes the same composition at :1246-1247. Those two compositions are textually identical, so the predicate really is single-definition and the two sides cannot disagree given equal inputs.

closures.item: (b) The 2^4 equality test compares the TWO CALL SITES' composition (D3 vacuity check)
closures.proof: WaveDTests.swift:495-532 compares `GeoARSessionManager.reconstructionDesired(...)` (:502-507) against `GeoARSessionManager.perceptionPlan(...).reconstruction` (:508-522). Since round 4 made perceptionPlan delegate verbatim to the predicate (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1374-1379), `viaPlan` IS `direct` by construction — the loop asserts f(x)==f(x) for all 16 rows. The resume side is never touched: resumeSession is a @MainActor instance method requiring an ARView and appears nowhere in the test file, and no test in the repo constructs ARSessionHolder or GeoARSessionManager (all 42 `GeoARSessionManager.` references in the test target are to nonisolated statics). The round-3 defect never lived in the predicate — it lived in the ARGUMENT composition and in the call ORDER in the restorers — and neither is asserted anywhere. DECISIONS.md's round-3 entry prescribed 'one shared reconstructionDesired predicate asserted equal across both sides'; the shared predicate landed, the cross-side assertion did not. See F-D4-01.

closures.item: (c) markCameraHidden hide-edge stamp × the reorder — can a fast hide→show flip double-run or skip the mesh rebuild decision?
closures.proof: Three flips walked. (1) Sub-pause flip (hide t=0, show t=1): cameraDidDisappear → markCameraHidden (:598-609) stamps lastCameraVisibleAt=0 and cancels the drag; the pause task (ARSessionHolder.swift:115-125) is still pending, sessionRunning stays true, so cameraDidAppear's startIfNeeded hits `attached && sessionRunning` and does nothing — resumeSession is never entered, so the reorder cannot double-run here. Ticks in the gap keep reconstruction TRUE because cameraRecentlyVisible(now, 0) holds through t=6.0 (:487, :1246-1247) — the mesh is never destroyed and never rebuilt, which is ARPCFG-4's intent. (2) Flip across the pause (hide t=0, suspend t=5, show t=5.1): resumeSession's first disjunct `cameraVisible` is already TRUE from the reorder, so the fallback is not even consulted — one run, and the first tick agrees. (3) Long-gap show (hide t=0, show t=20): cameraVisible=true dominates the stale stamp, reconstruction TRUE, one run. There is no ordering in which the hide-edge stamp and the reorder can both be wrong: markCameraHidden and markCameraVisible are the only two edge writers and they are mutually exclusive on the main actor, and the per-tick refresh at :1187 is gated on cameraVisible so it can never resurrect a stale stamp after a hide. No skipped rebuild decision found.

closures.item: (d) NEW ordering hazards introduced by the reorder
closures.proof: Swept every state markCameraVisible writes (GeoARSessionManager.swift:614-621) against everything startIfNeeded can now run after it. `cameraVisible`: read by resumeSession (:573), updatePowerTier (:1187, :1206, :1245-1246), frameUpdate consumers (:2531) — none run inside the same synchronous block, and attach/runGPSCompass/decideModeAndRun read it nowhere. `cameraVisibleAt`: only recordTTFOIfNeeded (:2309), tolerant of the microsecond shift. `timeToFirstObjectMs`: attach (:328) overwrites it, which is correct on a first attach (placedHolders empty ⇒ markCameraVisible also wrote nil) and unreachable on any other path since `detach()` has no callers. The early-return in startIfNeeded (ARSessionHolder.swift:101) leaves cameraVisible=true with no session, but that was equally true before the reorder (markCameraVisible ran unconditionally either way) and no tick exists to read it. Both restorers are now identical in shape, so the two call sites cannot drift apart by inspection. No new hazard found.

findings.claim: testResumeAndTickReconstructionCanNeverDisagree is VACUOUS with respect to F-D3-02: it compares reconstructionDesired against perceptionPlan, which since round 4 delegates to reconstructionDesired verbatim (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1374-1379), so all 16 rows assert f(x)==f(x). Reverting EITHER F-D3-02 hunk — the markCameraVisible/startIfNeeded reorder in ARSessionHolder.swift:68-69 and :95-96, or the resumePlan composition at GeoARSessionManager.swift:571-577 — leaves this test green; no assertion trips, because the test never references resumeSession or ARSessionHolder. The HIGH is closed in the code and unguarded in the suite.
findings.harm: Field-measurable regression risk with a green suite. Any future edit that puts manager.markCameraVisible() back after startIfNeeded() — a merge, a 'tidy the restorers' refactor, or a new restorer copied from the pre-round-4 shape — silently restores the exact round-3 defect: every warm resume (tab return, phone call, app switch) runs session.run without .sceneReconstruction(.mesh) and the governor tick 0-400 ms later runs it again with mesh, destroying and rebuilding the LiDAR mesh at the reveal instant (multi-second occlusion holes, and 'Place on ground' raycasting an empty mesh right after resume). The 146/146 record and the DECISIONS.md claim 'asserted equal across both sides' would both continue to read green. This is a verbatim repeat of the round-3 lesson the counsel itself named: the suite is green because no test constructs the manager or the holder.
findings.fix: Give the reorder a seam and assert the ORDER, not the predicate. Extract a minimal port the holder talks to (protocol ARManagerPort { func markCameraVisible(); func markCameraHidden(); func resumeSession(); func attach(...) }), have ARSessionHolder hold it, and inject a recorder double in tests. Separately, extract the resume composition into a nonisolated static (e.g. resumeReconstruction(supports:cameraVisibleNow:lastVisible:now:pedestrian:thermalCritical:)) so the 2^4 table can compare resumePlan's composition to perceptionPlan's instead of the predicate to itself. Keep the existing 16-row loop as a drift guard but stop citing it as the F-D3-02 guard in DECISIONS.md.
findings.test_case: Caller-context, not literal-fed: drive the real ARSessionHolder lifecycle against a recording ARManagerPort double. Test 1 (warm tab return): configure(locationService:library:) → cameraDidAppear() → cameraDidDisappear() → advance past AppConfig.pauseGraceSeconds so the pause task calls suspendSession → cameraDidAppear(); assert the recorded call log contains markCameraVisible strictly before resumeSession, and that the port saw exactly one resumeSession. Test 2 (background→foreground): same setup, then appDidEnterBackground() → appDidBecomeActive(); same two assertions. Test 3 (double-run counter): give the double a real GeoARSessionManager-shaped stub that records every session.run-equivalent, seed it pedestrian + mesh-capable + non-critical, and assert exactly ONE configuration application across resume plus the first governor tick. Reverting either ARSessionHolder hunk flips the recorded order and trips Test 1/Test 2; reverting the resumePlan composition trips Test 3.

findings.claim: The `cameraVisible || Self.cameraRecentlyVisible(...)` composition in resumePlan is dead on both restorer paths (after the reorder the first disjunct is already true there) and is load-bearing ONLY on beginRevealWarmup, where it is wrong for the grace tail: for a warmup resume landing between t=pauseGraceSeconds (5.0 s, when the pause fires and sessionRunning goes false) and t=6.0 s after the hide edge, cameraRecentlyVisible is still true (:487), so the resume requests .sceneReconstruction(.mesh) with the camera surface provably off-screen; the governor tick that crosses t=6.0 then computes reconstruction=false (:1246-1247, :1374) and setPerception (:882-896) fires a SECOND session.run within one to two 400 ms ticks. The comment at :566-569 claiming 'one session.run, including on the beginRevealWarmup path inside the grace window' is false for that tail.
findings.harm: Field-measurable and bounded but real: up to ~1 s of LiDAR meshing with no visible camera surface on the exact path ADR-033's idle diet exists to protect (a deep link or onboarding reveal arriving 5-6 s after the user leaves the camera tab — ReceiveScreen.swift:50, OnboardingView.swift:154), followed by a mesh build→teardown cycle immediately before the user taps 'Reveal in AR', where the tick then re-requests mesh. Observable in the metrics log as a 'Perception recon=false person=false depth=false' line within ~1 s of a warmup resume that had just configured mesh. It is strictly better than round 3 (which double-ran in the same sliver in the opposite direction), so this is a comment-overclaim plus a narrow leftover, not a regression.
findings.fix: Either drop the fallback disjunct from resumePlan (leaving raw `cameraVisible`, which is now correct on every restorer path and makes the warmup resume honestly idle), or keep it and correct the comment at :566-569 to say the agreement holds only while the grace is live. If the fallback is kept, gate it on the remaining grace exceeding one tick — e.g. require `cameraRecentlyVisible(now: Date().addingTimeInterval(0.4), lastVisible: lastCameraVisibleAt)` so the resume never requests a stream the very next tick will shed.
findings.test_case: Pure, caller-context: extract resumeReconstruction(supports:cameraVisibleNow:lastVisible:now:pedestrian:thermalCritical:) and assert the no-shed invariant across the boundary — for cameraVisibleNow=false and lastVisible = now - (pauseGraceSeconds + 0.5), assert resumeReconstruction(...) equals perceptionPlan(...).reconstruction evaluated at now + 0.8 s with the same lastVisible (i.e. the resume must not request what the next-but-one tick sheds). Sweep the offset from grace+0.0 to grace+1.5 in 0.1 s steps so the failing sliver is located, not just detected. Field leg: add to FIELDTESTS an assertion that a warmup resume with the camera hidden emits no 'Perception recon=' line within 2 s.

test_vacuity.reason: VACUOUS for F-D3-02. `viaPlan` is computed through perceptionPlan, which since GeoARSessionManager.swift:1374-1379 delegates verbatim to reconstructionDesired — so the single assertion XCTAssertEqual(direct, viaPlan) is a tautology on all 16 rows. Revert the ARSessionHolder reorder (:68-69, :95-96): test still passes, no assertion trips. Revert resumePlan back to raw `cameraVisible` (:571-577): test still passes — resumeSession is never called. Revert perceptionPlan's delegation to the round-3 inline `supports && recent && pedestrian && !critical`: test STILL passes, because that expression is character-identical to the predicate body. The only mutation it catches is someone writing a genuinely different formula inline in perceptionPlan, which the delegation already prevents.

Genuinely guards the (c) mechanism. Against the round-2 form (`< AppConfig.pauseGraceSeconds`, no +1.0), the interval at pauseMoment is exactly 5.0 and `5.0 < 5.0` is false, so XCTAssertTrue at :432 ('the grace covers the pause moment itself') trips, and :435 ('…and a full 400 ms tick of drift past it') trips too. The negative bound at :438 also binds — an unbounded grace would fail it. Unchanged by round 4, but it is the reason the reorder's fallback path stays honest.

Its only assertion, XCTAssertGreaterThanOrEqual(observedActive, 0), is a tautology on a counter that starts at 0 and only increments — outside a sanitizer run it can fail only by crashing. Its value is entirely as the TSan probe the RSCH-1 amendment names it as, and even there the coverage is narrower than the amendment implies: the pass is constructed without prepare(on:), so `arView` is nil and setCallbacksActive returns at the `guard changed, let arView` (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:195) before ever touching arView.renderCallbacks. It exercises stateLock around callbacksActiveStorage (:172-194) and releaseCaptureResources only — consistent with the amendment's own 'honest unknown' about the slot assignment, but DECISIONS.md should say the probe does not reach that code.

residuals: The `|| Self.cameraRecentlyVisible(...)` disjunct at GeoARSessionManager.swift:574 is now DEAD on both restorer paths (cameraVisible is already true there after the reorder) and live only on beginRevealWarmup — worth a one-line comment correction so a future reader does not believe it is the general resume mechanism. Can wait: the code is correct on the paths that matter; only the comment overstates reach.

suspendSession (GeoARSessionManager.swift:423-444) sets cameraVisible=false at :426 without stamping lastCameraVisibleAt, so the hide edge has two writers (markCameraHidden :604, the per-tick refresh :1187) and one silent non-writer. Harmless today because the background→foreground path always calls markCameraVisible before resumeSession, but it means the stamp on that path is up to 400 ms stale. Can wait: the staleness is bounded by one tick and the grace already carries +1.0 s of margin for exactly this.

No test in the repo constructs ARSessionHolder or GeoARSessionManager — all 42 test references are to nonisolated statics. Round 3's named lesson (green suite, dead flagship button) is structurally unaddressed after round 4; F-D4-01 is the concrete instance but the gap is general (nothing guards markCameraHidden→cancelLiveEdit, the pause-task lifecycle, or the attach/resume branch selection either). Can wait past this round only if the counsel accepts the seam work as a scheduled item rather than a blocker.

FIELDTESTS.md gained FT-40 for the F-D3-01 ground-snap case but nothing for F-D3-02 — there is no field assertion that a warm resume produces exactly one configuration change. A one-line FT ('after a tab return, the metrics log shows no \'Perception recon=\' line within 1 s of Resuming…') would make the HIGH observable in the field run. Can wait: the mechanism is closed by inspection; this is confirmation, not detection.
reviews.ship_opinion: F-D3-02 is genuinely CLOSED at mechanism level on every reachable resume that matters: both restorers now mark visibility before startIfNeeded (ARSessionHolder.swift:68-69, :95-96), resumeSession's first disjunct is therefore TRUE at GeoARSessionManager.swift:573, and the shared reconstructionDesired predicate (:494-502) is the single definition consumed by both the resume plan (:571) and the tick plan (:1374), so the warm resume and the first governor tick compute the same tuple and setPerception's identity guard (:884) collapses it to exactly one session.run. I found no new ordering hazard from the reorder — attach-first-run does not reach resumeSession, markCameraVisible writes nothing attach depends on, and detach() has no callers so re-attach is unreachable. Round 4 is close-able on my item. What is NOT delivered is the second half of round 3's prescription: the 2^4 table at WaveDTests.swift:495 asserts the predicate against itself through perceptionPlan's verbatim delegation, never against resumePlan's composition and never against the call order that was the actual bug — so the HIGH is fixed and unguarded, and DECISIONS.md's 'asserted equal across both sides' currently overstates the suite. That is a MEDIUM, not a blocker: it does not change what ships, it changes whether the next diff can silently unship it. My recommendation for the field-run gate: let the wave proceed, but do not sign the round-4 record with the current wording — either land the recording-port call-order test before the field run, or amend DECISIONS.md and FIELDTESTS.md to state plainly that F-D3-02 is verified by inspection only and add the one-line field assertion (no 'Perception recon=' line within 1 s of 'Resuming…') so the field run is the evidence the suite is not. The beginRevealWarmup grace-tail sliver (F-D4-02) is a LOW comment-overclaim plus a bounded 1 s leftover and should not hold the gate.

closures.item: (a) heldGestures — every increment/decrement/zeroing site enumerated; counter cannot go permanently positive (round-1 governor-pinned-.full heat blocker) nor negative-then-clamped
closures.proof: COMPLETE SITE LIST, all read in /Users/captiveon/Documents/techproject/experimental/thmillion/practical/AugmentMeReality/AugmentMeReality/AR/GeoARSessionManager.swift. Declaration :248 `private var heldGestures = 0`; derived :249 `private var gestureHeld: Bool { heldGestures > 0 }`. INCREMENT — exactly one: :452 `heldGestures = min(heldGestures + 1, 4)` in beginLiveEdit, whose only callers are the three sliders' onEditingChanged(true) at ARScreen.swift:504, :531, :558 (grep over all *.swift confirms no fourth caller). DECREMENT — exactly one: :2014 `heldGestures = max(0, heldGestures - 1)` in adjustNearestDrop, hoisted ABOVE the applyEdit call at :2016 so the unresolved-drop early return at :2030-2035 can no longer strand it (the round-3 defect). ZEROING — exactly three: :461 cancelLiveEdit (placed BEFORE the `guard editingDropID != nil || !liveEditingDrops.isEmpty` at :462, so it always executes), :921 resetPlacements, :1633 removePerDropState under `if editingDropID == id`. NEGATIVE: impossible — :2014 is the sole decrement and is max(0,·)-clamped; and it is unreachable with an empty count in the leak shapes, because a commit only reaches :2014 after editTarget (:2005-2008) returns non-nil, which with capture==nil requires held==true i.e. heldGestures>0. So the clamp is never load-bearing and cannot mask a leak. PERMANENTLY POSITIVE / governor pin: the governor reads liveEditingDrops, not heldGestures (:1211 `isLiveEditing: !liveEditingDrops.isEmpty`). Every path that can strand a liveEditingDrops entry now terminates in cancelLiveEdit within 30 s of the last value tick, because the round-4 backstop at :1181 is `if editingDropID != nil || gestureHeld` (Swift parses this as (capture||held) && gestureAbandoned, comma = AND) and updatePowerTier runs every 400 ms tick (:1078 sleep 400_000_000 → :1110). The one path where ticking stops is suspendSession, which itself calls cancelLiveEdit at :441. Saturation is also self-draining, not latching: at heldGestures==4 a begin is a no-op (min(5,4)=4) while the matching commit still decrements to 3, so the cap can only push the counter DOWN, never strand it up. The round-1 blocker (governor pinned .full for the rest of the session) is genuinely dead; bounded at ≤30 s. Residual (not a blocker): a phantom count can survive arbitrarily long if the user touches a slider at least once per 30 s — see residuals.

closures.item: (c) D3 on CallerClockTests.testHeldGestureIsNeverAbandonedByTickSilence — does it drive the caller's Date arithmetic for round-4 counter semantics?
closures.proof: The rows at /Users/captiveon/Documents/techproject/experimental/thmillion/practical/AugmentMeReality/AugmentMeRealityTests/WaveDTests.swift:406-423 are NON-VACUOUS for what they actually guard: they hand Date pairs (not literal intervals) to GeoARSessionManager.gestureAbandoned (:472-477), and reverting the predicate to round 2's unconditional `silent > 1.5` trips :411-413 ("10 s of stationary hold is a drag, not abandonment"); deleting the 30 s backstop trips :414-416. That much survives. But they are VACUOUS as a guard on anything round 4 touched: gestureAbandoned's signature and body are byte-identical across 91216b7..6d50ca4 (the diff shows no hunk in that range), the test passes a literal Bool for `held`, and nothing in the file ever constructs GeoARSessionManager — so no assertion can observe whether heldGestures is balanced, whether the decrement is hoisted, or whether :1181's new `|| gestureHeld` disjunct exists. Reverting the entire round-4 counter to round 3's stored Bool leaves 146/146 green. PREMISE INVALIDATION: the counter did quietly weaken the caller-side premise of the two `held: false` rows (:417-422, "an unheld capture is truly abandoned and expires fast"). In round 3 `gestureHeld` was cleared by the commit itself, so held==false was the normal post-gesture state and 1.5 s was the live expiry. In round 4 held==false requires the counter to reach zero, and any phantom (see residuals) keeps it at ≥1 indefinitely — in those states the caller passes held:true forever and the 1.5 s row describes a branch the caller can no longer enter. The row is still arithmetically true and still worth keeping; it just no longer certifies the fast expiry is live in the field. closures.item: (d) removePerDropState — the round-4 heldGestures zeroing (plus the round-2 nearestDrop clear and geospatial.invalidateAnchor) cannot fire during a live gesture on a DIFFERENT drop and strand its decrement
closures.proof: GeoARSessionManager.swift:1617-1649. Provenance first: `git diff 91216b7..6d50ca4` shows the ONLY round-4 addition here is `heldGestures = 0` at :1633; the nearestDrop clear (:1641-1644) and geospatial.invalidateAnchor (:1648) are round-2 lines carried unchanged — the assignment's premise that all three are round-4 additions is not what the diff says. STRANDING: impossible for a different drop. The zeroing is inside `if editingDropID == id` (:1629), and the capture is a single scalar that can only be written at :454 (begin, only when nil), :2009 (tick bind) and cleared at :2032/:2099/:464/:920/:1630 — so a concurrent gesture is ALWAYS bound to the same id as the capture (begin #2 hits the `if editingDropID == nil` guard at :454 and leaves the capture alone). Therefore removePerDropState(Y) with Y != capture touches neither heldGestures nor the live gesture's decrement path; removePerDropState(X) with X == capture zeroes a count whose every finger was bound to X, and the subsequent releases are refused at :2005-2008 (capture nil, held false) so no decrement is owed. The `nearestDrop?.id == id` clear at :1641 is likewise identity-gated. The call sites are the per-tick reconcile loops (:1899, :2438) and clearRoomDrops (:700), all of which pass ids drawn from placedHolders/roomDrops — none can pass a foreign id. NOTE, positively: this line closes a genuine round-3 hole. Before it, a drop deleted under a live finger cleared the capture but left gestureHeld true, so the very next tick took the `held ? nearest : nil` branch and wrote the user's drag into whatever drop nearest had become. That wrong-drop write is now dead for this path.

closures.item: F-D3-04 as stated — 'one boolean couldn't represent two concurrent thumb gestures (committing one slider killed a still-live drag on another)'
closures.proof: The COUNT is now a depth counter, but the CAPTURE is still a scalar that the first commit destroys unconditionally: GeoARSessionManager.swift:2099 `if editingDropID == id { editingDropID = nil }` runs inside applyEdit with no reference to heldGestures. So round 4 converted 'the surviving drag is killed' into 'the surviving drag silently re-binds to whatever nearest has become' — the same wrong-drop persist family the counter was introduced to kill. Full trace in finding F-D4-01. The counter's stated purpose is therefore half-delivered; the fix is ~3 lines.

findings.claim: The capture teardown `if editingDropID == id { editingDropID = nil }` at :2099 (and the twin at :2032) lives inside applyEdit and ignores heldGestures, so the FIRST commit of a multi-thumb interaction destroys the shared capture while other fingers are still down — and the authored path (snapNearestDropToGround → applyEdit at :2186) destroys it too, in direct contradiction of applyEdit's own doc contract at :2019-2021 ('programmatic (authored) callers commit to an explicit target with no gesture state read or written'). With the capture gone, updateNearest unfreezes at :1655 and the surviving gesture's next tick takes editTarget's `return held ? nearest : nil` branch (:513) and re-binds to a DIFFERENT drop.
findings.harm: A wrong-drop edit persisted to disk and Firestore. Trigger A (two thumbs, no button): drops X and Y both nearby, X nearest. Thumb1 presses the height slider (ARScreen.swift:504 → :452 heldGestures=1, :454 capture=X). Thumb2 presses the rotation slider (ARScreen.swift:558 → heldGestures=2, capture stays X). Thumb1 lifts (ARScreen.swift:506 commit) → :2014 heldGestures→1, :2099 capture=nil with thumb2 still down. Within one 400 ms tick (:1078/:1107) updateNearest reassigns nearestDrop=Y. Thumb2 keeps rotating (ARScreen.swift:548) → editTarget(capture:nil, held:true, nearest:Y) → Y → :2009 capture=Y → applyEdit rotates Y; thumb2 lifts → commit → :2082-2094 `library.update(edited, persist: true)` writes drop Y's facing with the value the user aimed at X. Simultaneously ARScreen.swift:601 onChange(of: nearestDrop?.id) fires syncSliders and the thumb's slider visibly snaps mid-drag. Trigger B (one thumb + one tap, no second slider needed): finger holds any slider; a second finger taps 'Place on ground' (ARScreen.swift:571) → snapNearestDropToGround → applyEdit(to: X, commit: true) at :2186 → :2099 clears the capture out from under the live finger, heldGestures stays 1, and the same re-bind window opens. findings.fix: Make the capture teardown a property of the gesture count, and take it out of the mutation. In adjustNearestDrop replace the commit block at :2011-2015 with `if commit { heldGestures = max(0, heldGestures - 1); if heldGestures == 0, editingDropID == id { editingDropID = nil } }`, and DELETE the capture writes from applyEdit (:2032 and :2099) so applyEdit finally honours its documented contract of touching no gesture state. Keep `liveEditingDrops.remove(id)` at :2098/:2033 where it is (it is per-drop, not per-gesture). Optionally add a `captureSurvives(held:)` one-liner alongside editTarget so the invariant is table-testable.

validations.claim: (a) Thread Sanitizer does not exist for physical iOS devices — no configuration of this project can ever execute it.
validations.basis: Primary source is the installed toolchain, not documentation: `ls /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Toolchains/XcodeDefault.xctoolchain/usr/lib/clang/21/lib/darwin | grep tsan` on Xcode 26.6 (17F113) returns exactly libclang_rt.tsan_iossim_dynamic.dylib, tsan_osx, tsan_tvossim, tsan_watchossim, tsan_xros, tsan_xrossim. There is NO libclang_rt.tsan_ios_dynamic.dylib — the device-iOS TSan runtime does not ship, so the linker has nothing to embed and the scheme toggle has nothing to enable. Corroborated by Apple's 'Diagnosing memory, thread, and crash issues early': you cannot use Thread Sanitizer to diagnose iOS/tvOS/watchOS apps running on a device; it is supported only for 64-bit macOS and 64-bit iOS/tvOS Simulators. The exit condition was correctly declared void.

validations.claim: (a, reason clause) 'Apple's runtime ships no arm64e-device TSan library.'
validations.basis: Same directory listing: libclang_rt.tsan_xros_dynamic.dylib IS present — that is a TSan runtime for visionOS *device* (arm64), and libclang_rt.tsan_osx_dynamic.dylib covers arm64 macOS. So Apple does ship device-arm64 TSan runtimes; it just does not ship one for iOS. The true statement is narrower and stronger: no iOS-device TSan runtime exists in any shipping Xcode, which makes it a platform-support decision rather than a technical impossibility. Fix the clause to 'no iOS-device TSan runtime ships (the toolchain carries tsan_iossim, tsan_osx and tsan_xros, but no tsan_ios)' so the record cannot be dismissed by anyone who greps the same directory.

validations.claim: (b) ASan / UBSan / Zombie-Malloc diagnostics DO run on a physical iOS device.
validations.basis: Same toolchain directory contains libclang_rt.asan_ios_dynamic.dylib and libclang_rt.ubsan_ios_dynamic.dylib (device variants, alongside their _iossim siblings), and /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/iPhoneOS.platform/Developer/SDKs/iPhoneOS26.5.sdk/usr/lib/libgmalloc.tbd exists, i.e. Guard Malloc is linkable against the device SDK. Zombie Objects and Malloc Scribble/Guard Edges are env-var diagnostics in libsystem_malloc and are available on device. Main Thread Checker is a dylib inserted on device by Xcode and is likewise fine. Leg 2 is executable exactly as written.

validations.claim: (b, scope) Leg 2's stated purpose: device ASan/UBSan 'catches the consequences (use-after-free, torn reads that dereference) even where the race itself is invisible' — as cover for the RENDER-1 renderCallbacks unknown.
validations.basis: First-principles limit of ASan's design (clang.llvm.org/docs/AddressSanitizer.html model): ASan validates only loads and stores in code compiled with -fsanitize=address, by checking a shadow map at each instrumented access. RealityKit is a prebuilt system framework and is never rebuilt with ASan. The dangerous access in the honest unknown — RealityKit's render thread reading arView.renderCallbacks.postProcess while the main actor nils it and releases the closure context box — happens entirely inside uninstrumented Apple code, so ASan cannot check it. Leg 2 is genuinely valuable for the app's own memory bugs (SemanticOcclusionPass texture wrappers, PersonSentinel buffer retention) but it provably cannot cover the RENDER-1 residual, and the record should not imply it does.

validations.claim: (c) A 17.x-era simulator aborts in dyld while loading the TSan runtime, while a 26.x simulator works — mechanism: mismatched libclang_rt.tsan_iossim_dynamic vs old simulator runtime.
validations.basis: Mechanism is documented with the exact signature in Apple Developer Forums thread 686884 ('App launch fails with Thread Sanitiser enabled'): `dyld: Symbol not found: _vfork / Referenced from: .../libclang_rt.tsan_iossim_dynamic.dylib / Expected in: /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib`. The TSan runtime shipped with the current toolchain forward-references libSystem symbols that older simulator runtimes' libSystem does not export, so dyld aborts at load. That is precisely the mechanism the record posits, and the environment here is consistent: `xcrun simctl list runtimes` shows iOS 17.0, iOS 17.2 and iOS 26.5 installed, so an unqualified `name=iPhone 17 Pro` destination can and will resolve against an old runtime.

validations.claim: (c, boundary) The specific claim that '17.x-era simulators' are the failing generation.
validations.basis: The published failure boundary in thread 686884 is iOS <=14.4 simulator fails / >=15.2 works; I found no public report pinning a 17.x boundary against an Xcode 26 toolchain. The 17.x abort is therefore an operator observation on this machine, not a citable fact. It is almost certainly the same _vfork-class forward-reference, but the record should either paste the actual dyld error text observed locally or state the mechanism ('the TSan runtime forward-references libSystem symbols absent from older simulator runtimes — always use a current-OS simulator') instead of a version number that a reader cannot check.

validations.claim: (d) SecItemAdd -34018 is a missing-entitlement artifact of CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO simulator builds, not an app bug.
validations.basis: -34018 is errSecMissingEntitlement (Security framework OSStatus). Apple Developer Forums 4743 and 64699 establish the shape: the data-protection keychain gates access on entitlements; the Simulator substitutes *simulated* entitlements because macOS refuses to run a bundle carrying real ones, and a build with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO carries no keychain-access-group entitlement at all, so SecItemAdd returns -34018. The reasoning is sound here specifically because the record pairs it with 'the same test passes on device' (146/146 signed device run) — that pairing is what makes it an environment artifact rather than a latent bug, since -34018 is ALSO the device symptom of a stale/missing keychain-access-group entitlement. Keep the device-pass sentence attached to the claim; it is load-bearing, not decoration.

validations.claim: (e, status) 'Mitigated, not proven' is the right epistemic status for the renderCallbacks slot-assignment unknown.
validations.basis: Correct and appropriately humble. The residual is real: SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:195-206 writes arView.renderCallbacks.prepareWithDevice and .postProcess OUTSIDE stateLock (released at :194), and a Swift closure value is a two-word {function pointer, context reference} pair whose assignment is neither atomic nor ordered, with a release of the previous context on overwrite — the detach direction is the crash-shaped one. The round-3 dwell floor (idle >5 s AND attached >10 s) reduces the number of windows per session to single digits but changes nothing about the window itself. No dynamic tool available to this project can observe it: device TSan does not exist (a), simulator TSan never runs RealityKit's render thread, and ASan does not instrument RealityKit (b-scope). 'Mitigated, not proven' is exactly right.

validations.claim: (e, framing) The record's terminal condition: 'no public API... this line stays until RealityKit exposes a synchronization point for callback swaps.'
validations.basis: Two corrections, one that strengthens the record and one that removes a dead end. (1) UNDERSTATED: ARView.renderCallbacks is a @MainActor-isolated property (ARView is a UIView subclass), and this app writes it ONLY from @MainActor code — SemanticOcclusionPass is @unchecked Sendable but every call site is inside @MainActor GeoARSessionManager (declared @MainActor at :25; call sites :397, :418, :1323, :1330). The app therefore uses the API exactly as Apple's declared isolation prescribes; the residual is whether RealityKit synchronizes its own render-thread read of a property it publishes as main-actor-isolated. That is a platform contract question, not an app defect, and it should be recorded as such with a filed Feedback Assistant FB number — a filed FB is the only mechanism that can ever discharge a condition worded 'until RealityKit exposes a synchronization point'. (2) I checked the candidate synchronization points and confirm none is usable: Apple's own docs (fetched rendercallbacks-swift.struct.json) state only WHEN the callbacks fire ('every frame, after RealityKit renders the scene, but before it displays it') with no threading, re-entrancy or thread-safety contract; session.pause() is NOT a quiescence point — the app's own verified comment at GeoARSessionManager.swift:2498 records that 'RealityKit keeps rendering (and firing SceneEvents) on a frozen or dead camera'; and writing the slot from inside postProcess would violate the property's main-actor isolation. What the record DOES ignore is the app-side elimination: install-once + a lock-protected flag inside encode, rejected by ADR-035 on a heat measurement that this counsel's own Wave D round 1 verdict already recorded as STALE (it predates the shader early-out at SemanticMatte.metal:147-172 and the bare-blit idle path at SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:427-431). 'No public API exists' is true; 'nothing the app can do' is false, and the record should name the ADR-035 re-measurement as the open app-side exit.

validations.claim: Leg 1 (simulator TSan) covers 'PersonSentinel's lock discipline across the queue boundary and SemanticOcclusionPass's stateLock usage', with SemanticPassCrossThreadTests as the designed cross-thread probe.
validations.basis: Falsified by the suite itself. `grep -rn PersonSentinel AugmentMeRealityTests/` returns nothing — the sentinel is never instantiated by any test, so TSan observed zero of its cross-queue state (busy/lastRunAt/lastSeenAt/lastLongHoldLogAt). `grep -rn 'ARSessionHolder|GeoARSessionManager('` over the test target likewise returns nothing. And the one probe that does exist, WaveDTests.swift:535-555, constructs SemanticOcclusionPass without ever calling prepare(on:), so arView is nil and the `guard changed, let arView else { return }` at SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:195 returns before the renderCallbacks assignment — the exact code the honest unknown is about is never executed. As executed, leg 1 proves that one Bool (callbacksActiveStorage) behind one NSLock is race-free. The round-3 checklist stated this conditionally and correctly ('IF a test drives them from two threads'); the amendment dropped the condition. TSan is a dynamic tool: its coverage is exactly the concurrency the tests actually perform.

validations.claim: Leg 3: 'every stateLock acquisition is leaf-level (no callouts while held), enforced by the round-1 audit'.
validations.basis: Literally false against the code it certifies. SemanticOcclusionPass.setCallbacksActive holds stateLock across releaseCaptureResources() (:185-194), which calls CVMetalTextureCacheFlush (:453-458); uninstall() does the same (:214-219); and encode() holds stateLock across the ENTIRE CPU-side encode (:263-268 'the WHOLE CPU-side encode holds the state lock'), including CVMetalTextureCacheCreateTextureFromImage via makeTexture (:278-279). Those are callouts into CoreVideo/Metal under the lock. The property that IS true and checkable is the weaker one that actually matters: no *in-app* lock is acquired while stateLock is held, so no in-app lock-order inversion is constructible, and the only calls under it are leaf CoreVideo/Metal wrappers. Restate leg 3 in those terms or it fails the first reader who opens the file.

validations.claim: '145/146 pass' is evidence of 'zero ThreadSanitizer: data race reports'.
validations.basis: Pass count and race count are different measurements. Per clang.llvm.org/docs/ThreadSanitizer.html and the google/sanitizers ThreadSanitizerFlags reference, TSan defaults to halt_on_error=0 (report and continue) with exitcode=66 set at process exit if any warning fired. The propagation of exit 66 through the simulator test-runner into an xcodebuild failure is real-world flaky (cf. realm/SwiftLint #2089, ReactiveX/RxSwift #2145 where TSan issues surfaced inconsistently), and the probe's own assertion cannot fail regardless. The zero-reports claim is only as good as an explicit grep. Re-run leg 1 with TSAN_OPTIONS='halt_on_error=1' and record the evidence as 'grep -c "ThreadSanitizer:" <xcodebuild log> == 0', citing build 6d50ca4 — not as a pass count.

validations.claim: Round 4's own tests non-vacuously guard the two blockers it exists to close (D3).
validations.basis: Both PURE decisions are guarded; neither WIRING is. testEditTargetBindsInBothDirections (WaveDTests.swift:461-493) is non-vacuous for editTarget — assertion :467-471 (capture nil, held false, authored set -> authored) is precisely the round-3 refusal — but nothing anywhere asserts that snapNearestDropToGround (:2181) routes through applyEdit rather than adjustNearestDrop; `grep snapNearestDropToGround|applyEdit|adjustNearestDrop AugmentMeRealityTests/` is empty, so re-introducing F-D3-01 leaves all five assertions green. testResumeAndTickReconstructionCanNeverDisagree (:495-528) is non-vacuous for divergence between reconstructionDesired and perceptionPlan across the 2^4 table, but it passes `cameraVisible: recent` into both sides — it asserts the predicate, not the caller. Revert the ARSessionHolder reorder (:61-72, :90-97) and it still passes, because no test constructs ARSessionHolder. Consequence for the exit ruling: FT-40 and FT-3's 'no Perception recon= within 1 s of a >10 s return' are the ONLY guards on the two blockers, so they are gating measurements, not optional ones.

own_findings.claim: Leg 1 — the primary substitute for the exit condition that was voided — is credited with coverage the test suite does not have, and its one probe is structurally incapable of failing. WaveDTests.swift:536-539 builds SemanticOcclusionPass without prepare(on:), so arView is nil and SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:195 (`guard changed, let arView else { return }`) returns before the renderCallbacks assignment at :196-206 — the exact statement the honest unknown is about never runs under TSan. The sole assertion, XCTAssertGreaterThanOrEqual(observedActive, 0) at WaveDTests.swift:554, is a tautology on a non-negative Int. The reader loop at :549 is a fixed 2000 lock/unlock iterations on the calling thread with no rendezvous against the toggler dispatched at :542, so the reader can complete in microseconds before the background queue is even scheduled — a run containing zero actual concurrency is a legal outcome. And `grep -rn PersonSentinel AugmentMeRealityTests/` returns nothing, so the sentinel's cross-queue state (busy/lastRunAt/lastSeenAt/lastLongHoldLogAt) was never executed under the sanitizer at all.
own_findings.harm: The 99.5% crash-free bar gets signed against a leg that, as executed on 2026-08-18, proves exactly one Bool behind one NSLock is race-free. A future edit that removes stateLock from PersonSentinel, or reorders the renderCallbacks writes relative to the lock, produces the same green 145/146 and the same 'zero data race reports' line in DECISIONS.md. The record then reads as evidence when it is an absence of observation — the same failure shape as round 3's green suite with a dead 'Place on ground' button.
own_findings.fix: Three changes, all in the test target, ~30 lines. (1) Rendezvous and duration: a DispatchSemaphore the toggler signals before its loop, and run the reader against a deadline (`while Date() < end`) rather than a fixed count, so overlap is guaranteed. (2) Execute the slot write: call `pass.prepare(on: ARView(frame: .zero))` before toggling so :196-206 actually runs (simulator ARView construction is legal without a session). (3) Add a PersonSentinel two-queue probe that calls its analyze entry point from two queues while a reader reads the throttle state, so leg 1 covers the lock the round-3 verdict fixed. Then re-run leg 1 on 6d50ca4 with TSAN_OPTIONS='halt_on_error=1' and record `grep -c 'ThreadSanitizer:' <log> == 0` as the evidence, with the build SHA — TSan defaults to halt_on_error=0, so a pass count is not the measurement.

own_findings.claim: The amendment rests the crash bar on an instrument that does not exist in this build: 'the 99.5% crash bar therefore rests on legs (1)-(4) plus field crash telemetry.' There is no field crash telemetry. `grep -rn Crashlytics .` hits only DECISIONS.md:713; `grep -rn 'MetricKit|MXMetric' .` hits only a stray DECISIONS.md:159 mention and a round-2 archive suggestion. The Firebase package is linked for FirebaseAuth and FirebaseFirestore only (project.pbxproj:500-506) — Crashlytics is not a linked product. DECISIONS.md:713 already concedes the position in the project's own words: 'Crashlytics (BRIEF's 99.5% crash-free bar is currently unmeasurable)'.
own_findings.harm: Two harms. First, the record contradicts itself 489 lines apart — line 713 says the bar is unmeasurable, line 1202 says it rests partly on telemetry — and a wave cannot close honestly on a record that asserts both. Second, the protocol's actual crash evidence is 'zero AugmentMeReality-*.ips entries after one 70-minute session on one iPhone 15 Pro Max'. That is n=1 sessions against a fleet ratio; it cannot distinguish 99.5% crash-free from 95% crash-free. The RENDER-1 residual is precisely the kind of defect that appears once per several hundred sessions and never on the reviewer's phone — the bar most exposed to it is the one with no instrument.
own_findings.fix: Land MetricKit as the fifth leg before the field runs — it is first-party, ~30 lines, no SDK, no new package, and no privacy-manifest surface beyond what the app already declares. Conform an app-level object to MXMetricManagerSubscriber, register in didFinishLaunching, and persist didReceive(_ payloads: [MXDiagnosticPayload]): MXCrashDiagnostic gives the crash signature with a symbolicable call-stack tree, and MXHangDiagnostic is directly on-point for this wave because a main actor blocked behind SemanticOcclusionPass.stateLock during a render-thread encode manifests as a hang, not a crash, and would otherwise leave no trace at all. Also fold in MXAppRunTimeMetric so cumulative foreground time gives the denominator the crash ratio needs. Then rewrite the amendment's last sentence to say what is true: legs (1)-(5) plus MetricKit payloads are the pre-launch evidence, and the 99.5% ratio itself is explicitly deferred to TestFlight/production fleet data and is NOT signable from this protocol.

own_findings.claim: The amendment voided the unexecutable half of the original exit condition and silently dropped the executable half with it. The Wave D round 1 verdict specified the leg as TSan on device *with* SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY=complete (counsel-archives/wave-d-round1-verdict.json:68, :151, :908 — 'build the device target with -fsanitize=thread and SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY=complete'), and Wave C round 3 independently prescribed a warning-only complete lane as the documented incremental path (wave-c-round3-verdict.json:204, :208, :573). The project has never adopted it: project.pbxproj carries SWIFT_VERSION = 5.0 on all four configurations and no SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY setting anywhere, and there are no .xcconfig files. Default in Swift 5 mode is minimal, i.e. essentially unchecked.
own_findings.harm: The four-leg substitute is missing the one leg that is both fully executable today and exhaustive rather than sample-based. Every other leg is dynamic and therefore bounded by what a test or a walk happens to execute — which is exactly how RSCH4-01 got thin. Strict concurrency is static: it audits every isolation crossing in the codebase, including the two the wave is actually worried about (SemanticOcclusionPass is @unchecked Sendable with an NSLock, and DropStore's non-Sendable existential crossing that Wave C round 3 already documented at DropStore.swift:186-187/362). It is also the only leg that verifies the fact my validation of (e) leans on — that arView.renderCallbacks is written exclusively from main-actor context. Today nothing checks that; a future off-main call to setCallbacksActive would compile silently and turn the mitigated unknown into an unmitigated race.
own_findings.fix: Add leg 5 and run it before the field sessions: `xcodebuild -project AugmentMeReality.xcodeproj -scheme AugmentMeReality -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY=complete CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build 2>&1 | grep -c 'warning:.*concurrency\|warning:.*Sendable\|warning:.*actor-isolated'`. Warning-only, no source change, stays in Swift 5 mode, cannot break the build. Record the diagnostic count and triage only the ones naming SemanticOcclusionPass, PersonSentinel, GeoARSessionManager or DropStore; the rest go to Wave E with the existing Swift 6 migration debt. Add the line to the amendment as '(5) static isolation audit — the executable remainder of the original exit condition', so the record shows the TSan condition was replaced rather than reduced.

own_findings.claim: Leg 3's stated predicate is falsified by the code it certifies, and round 4 widened the exposure. 'Every stateLock acquisition is leaf-level (no callouts while held)' is contradicted by SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:185-194 (setCallbacksActive holds stateLock across releaseCaptureResources() -> CVMetalTextureCacheFlush at :453-458), :214-219 (uninstall, same), and above all :263-268, whose own comment states 'the WHOLE CPU-side encode holds the state lock' — including CVMetalTextureCacheCreateTextureFromImage via makeTexture at :278-279. Separately, round 4 added a new main-thread acquisition of that same lock: GeoARSessionManager.swift:1325 now evaluates `semanticPass?.callbacksActive == true` (which locks, SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:173-177) before calling setCallbacksActive at :1330 (which locks again), so a detach tick takes the render thread's lock twice from the main actor at 2.5 Hz.
own_findings.harm: Record harm: a leg substituting for an unexecutable exit condition is stated as a property that anyone opening the file disproves in thirty seconds, which discredits the other three legs by association. Field harm, bounded but real and on this wave's own bar: the main actor can block behind a full render-thread encode, and round 4 doubled the number of such acquisitions on the detach tick. That is a main-thread stall of exactly the shape MXHangDiagnostic (RSCH4-02) would report and that renderFPS's 2-second mean would smear away.
own_findings.fix: Two lines of record, zero lines of code. Restate leg 3 as the property that is true and mechanically checkable: 'no in-app lock is ever acquired while stateLock is held — the only calls under it are leaf CoreVideo/Metal wrappers — so no in-app lock-order inversion is constructible; re-verified each closure round by grepping every stateLock.lock() site (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:174, 185, 214, 228, 244, 267).' Optionally, and cheaply, collapse the round-4 double acquisition at GeoARSessionManager.swift:1325/1330 by having setCallbacksActive return the `changed` Bool and dropping the pre-check, so a detach tick takes the lock once.

own_findings.claim: The four-leg substitute has no instrument for the wave's fourth bar. BRIEF's bar is 'zero draw-over-known-front-surface FRAMES', but the only instrument in the protocol is a human: FT-3's 'count the seconds of draw-over before occlusion re-engages' and FT-9/FT-25/FT-27's visual pass. Nothing in the build logs an occlusion-coverage signal — the round-4 instruments added metricsLog lines for semantic-pass attach/detach (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1320, :1331) and gave PersonSentinel a subsystem (PersonSentinel.swift:23), neither of which says anything about whether content drew over a real surface on a given frame.
own_findings.harm: The bar is stated in frames and measured in seconds by memory, so it can only ever be signed as 'no visible hole', which is a materially weaker claim. The specific defect the bar exists to catch — F-D3-02's mesh teardown/rebuild signature on a warm resume — produces a hole at the reveal instant, when the observer is also being asked to watch the HUD, note the tier chip and time the return. A one-to-three-frame draw-over at 30 fps is 33-100 ms and is not reliably perceptible in real time; it IS perceptible on a scrubbed recording.
own_findings.fix: Turn on the iOS screen recorder (Control Centre) for every occlusion-bearing pass in Sessions 3 and 4 — each of the ten Camera<->Map >10 s returns, FT-9, FT-25, FT-27/FT-34, FT-29 — and scrub the resume moments frame by frame afterwards. Zero cost, no code, and it converts the wave's least-arguable bar into a reviewable artifact attached to the verdict rather than an operator's recollection. Note the one caveat in the record: ReplayKit capture adds GPU load, so the recording runs during FT-3/FT-9/FT-25/FT-27 (correctness passes) and must be OFF for the FT-28 fps/p95 window and the FT-31 thermal hour.

own_findings.claim: The two blockers this round exists to close have no automated guard on their wiring, only on their extracted predicates. `grep -rn 'ARSessionHolder|GeoARSessionManager('` over AugmentMeRealityTests/ returns nothing, and `grep -rn 'snapNearestDropToGround|applyEdit|adjustNearestDrop'` likewise returns nothing. So: reverting the F-D3-02 restorer reorder (ARSessionHolder.swift:61-72, :90-97) leaves testResumeAndTickReconstructionCanNeverDisagree green, because that test feeds `cameraVisible: recent` to both sides itself; and re-routing snapNearestDropToGround (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2181) back through adjustNearestDrop leaves all five assertions of testEditTargetBindsInBothDirections green. Additionally the round-3 verdict's closure list required 'the counter's floor-at-zero asserted' and a 147/147 target; the build is 146, and `grep -rn 'heldGestures|beginLiveEdit|cancelLiveEdit' AugmentMeRealityTests/` returns nothing — the F-D3-04 depth counter has zero coverage.

A green suite plus a green pure-predicate table is exactly the evidence configuration that let a CRITICAL dead flagship button survive a full counsel round. If either blocker regresses in Wave E, the suite will be green and the only detector is a field session someone has to remember to run. The heldGestures counter in particular is new, un-asserted, and sits on the persist path to disk and Firestore.

Add testHeldGestureCounterFloorsAtZero driving beginLiveEdit/cancelLiveEdit/commit sequences through the manager's own public entry points and asserting the counter never goes negative and reaches zero on cancel — that gets the build to the 147/147 the round-3 verdict specified. For the two wirings, do not build an ARView harness this round; instead record explicitly in the exit ruling that FT-40 (all five assertions, especially (d) survives force-quit) and FT-3's 'no "Perception recon=" line within ~1 s of a >10 s return' are the ONLY guards on F-D3-01 and F-D3-02 respectively, and are therefore gating measurements whose failure re-opens the wave. Carry an ARSessionHolder/manager test harness to Wave E as named debt.

'Leg 1 executed 2026-08-18 on the iOS 26.5 iPhone 17 Pro simulator: 145/146 pass' carries no commit SHA, while every other evidence line in DECISIONS.md is tied to a commit (e.g. 'Wave D round 3 BUILT (2026-08-17, 143/143 device tests)' and the round-3 verdict's explicit 'do not run FT-28 or FT-31 on cf3d43d').
