research.exit_ruling:
HONESTY: the amendment is honest in its core and I confirm its two hardest claims from primary sources. The TSan exit condition genuinely could never be discharged — Xcode 26.6's clang-21 toolchain ships libclang_rt.tsan_iossim/_osx/_tvossim/_watchossim/_xros/_xrossim and no libclang_rt.tsan_ios_dynamic.dylib, and Apple documents that TSan cannot diagnose iOS apps on device — so voiding it was correct and overdue, not a retreat. 'Mitigated, not proven' is the right status for the renderCallbacks residual, and I could not find a public synchronization point that the record missed: Apple's own ARView.RenderCallbacks documentation states only when the callbacks fire and gives no threading or thread-safety contract; session.pause() is not a quiescence point (the app's own verified comment at GeoARSessionManager.swift:2498 records that RealityKit keeps rendering and firing SceneEvents on a paused session); and writing the slot from the render thread would violate the property's main-actor isolation. ASan/UBSan/Guard-Malloc on device are real (asan_ios, ubsan_ios dylibs and iPhoneOS26.5.sdk libgmalloc.tbd all present), and -34018 is correctly diagnosed as errSecMissingEntitlement from an unsigned simulator build, made sound by the paired device pass.

COMPLETENESS: the record is NOT yet complete or accurate, in four specific ways, none of which requires re-litigating the code. (i) Leg 1 is credited with coverage the suite does not have — the cross-thread probe runs with arView nil so the renderCallbacks assignment at SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:196-206 never executes, its only assertion is a tautology, no test instantiates PersonSentinel, and the reader loop can finish before the toggler starts (RSCH4-01). (ii) The crash bar is rested on 'field crash telemetry' that is not in the build, contradicting DECISIONS.md:713's own 'currently unmeasurable' (RSCH4-02). (iii) Leg 3's stated predicate is disproved by the file it certifies — stateLock is held across CVMetalTextureCacheFlush and across the entire CPU-side encode (RSCH4-04). (iv) The executable half of the original round-1 exit condition, SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY=complete, was dropped along with the unexecutable TSan half; it remains unset (project.pbxproj SWIFT_VERSION = 5.0, no strict-concurrency key anywhere) despite being prescribed by two prior counsel rounds (RSCH4-03). Add it as leg 5. Two smaller repairs: the 'no arm64e-device TSan library' clause is wrong as written (tsan_xros and tsan_osx are arm64 device runtimes — the true claim is narrower and stronger: no iOS-device runtime ships), and the leg-1 evidence line needs the build SHA and a pinned OS in its destination (RSCH4-07).

THE FOUR-SESSION PROTOCOL AGAINST THE FOUR EMPIRICAL BARS:
1. Thermal, not .serious at 10 min — MEASURED, adequately. ProcessInfo.thermalState is read on the 2.5 Hz tick (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1490), latched into thermalSerious, surfaced as the banner (ARScreen.swift:468-469) so transients between samples are still caught, and logged with the active tier every 5 minutes (:1499-1501). FT-28 covers the 10-minute bar and FT-31 covers the hour. No gap.
2. Sustained >=30 fps — MEASURED, and the instrument is the right one; I checked this specifically because it is the easy thing to get wrong. frameCounter is incremented inside frameUpdate (:2510), which is the handler for the RealityKit render-loop subscription arView.scene.subscribe(to: SceneEvents.Update.self) established at :341 — not the ARSession delegate — so renderFPS (:1483-1487) measures presented render-loop frames, and p95 comes from a 240-sample interval ring (:2513-2519). Two caveats to record, both conservative (they under-report, never falsely pass): frameUpdate early-returns while interrupted/failed/non-gpsCompass (:2501), and renderFPS is a >=2-second mean, so sub-second hitching lives only in p95. Adopt the digest's proposed p95 <= 40 ms as the sustained bar's actual teeth; the mean alone cannot fail.
3. Zero draw-over-known-front-surface frames — NOT MEASURABLE at the stated granularity. The bar is in frames; the protocol's instrument is an operator counting seconds while simultaneously reading the HUD and timing a resume. A one-to-three-frame hole is 33-100 ms and is not reliably perceptible live. Fix is free and does not need a code change: screen-record every occlusion-bearing pass and scrub (RSCH4-05), with the recorder OFF during the FT-28 fps window and the FT-31 thermal hour.
4. >=99.5% crash-free — NOT MEASURABLE AT ALL, by this protocol or this build, and this is the ruling's headline. There is no crash telemetry linked (no Crashlytics product on the Firebase package at project.pbxproj:500-506, no MetricKit anywhere). The protocol's evidence is zero .ips files after ~2 hours on one device: necessary, and nowhere near sufficient for a fleet ratio. The round-3 digest says this plainly; the amendment must say it too instead of citing telemetry that does not exist.

WHAT REMAINS BEFORE WAVE D CAN CLOSE — in order, roughly two hours of desk work before anyone leaves the building:
A. Record repairs (no code): fix leg 1's coverage claim to what the probe executes; strike or qualify 'plus field crash telemetry'; restate leg 3 as 'no in-app lock is acquired while stateLock is held'; add leg 5 (static isolation audit) and note it is the executable remainder of the original condition; correct the arm64e clause; pin build 6d50ca4 and OS=26.5 on the leg-1 line; and file a Feedback Assistant report against RealityKit's undocumented render-thread read of the @MainActor-isolated renderCallbacks property, citing the FB number in the honest-unknown sentence — a condition worded 'until RealityKit exposes a synchronization point' cannot otherwise ever be discharged. Add one sentence naming the open app-side exit the record ignores: re-measure ADR-035's heat number (Wave D round 1 already recorded it as stale, predating SemanticMatte.metal:147-172 and SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:427-431) to decide whether install-once is now affordable, since install-once is the only construction that eliminates the unknown rather than mitigating it.
B. Cheap code, pre-field (~1 hour): rendezvous + prepare(on:) + duration-bounded reader in SemanticPassCrossThreadTests, a PersonSentinel two-queue probe, testHeldGestureCounterFloorsAtZero (which restores the round-3 verdict's 147/147 target, currently 146), and the MetricKit MXCrashDiagnostic/MXHangDiagnostic subscriber — MXHangDiagnostic is the one that would catch the main-actor block behind stateLock that renderFPS's 2-second mean smears away.
C. Re-run leg 1 on 6d50ca4 with TSAN_OPTIONS='halt_on_error=1' and record `grep -c 'ThreadSanitizer:' <log> == 0`, not a pass count. Run leg 5 and record the diagnostic count.
D. Then the four sessions, all on 6d50ca4, with the screen recorder on for every occlusion pass. Sessions 1 and 2 measure none of the four bars — Session 1 is a build/test gate and Session 2 is explicitly correctness-only (ASan's 2-3x CPU makes any fps or thermal number from it meaningless, which the digest already states). Session 3 carries bars 2 and 3 and the FT-40 regression case; Session 4 carries bar 3 over the hour plus ten more resume observations for bar 4's visual half.
E. Close on: 147/147 device green; leg 1 re-run clean by grep; leg 5 diagnostics recorded and the SemanticOcclusionPass/PersonSentinel/GeoARSessionManager/DropStore subset triaged; Session 2 zero reports; FT-28 fps steady with p95 recorded against the <=40 ms working bar and no thermal banner; FT-31 one hour with no banner and the chip timeline correct; FT-40 all five assertions including survival of force-quit; zero draw-over frames on scrubbed video across all ten resumes and FT-9/FT-25/FT-27; and — stated explicitly in the closing DECISIONS.md line rather than implied — the 99.5% crash-free ratio RE-SCOPED as a post-TestFlight fleet statistic that this protocol does not and cannot sign, with MetricKit landed as the mechanism that will eventually sign it.
Two gating measurements to flag loudly for the owner, because the suite cannot cover them (RSCH4-06): FT-40 is the only guard on F-D3-01 and FT-3's 'no \"Perception recon=\" within ~1 s of a >10 s return' is the only guard on F-D3-02. `grep` over AugmentMeRealityTests confirms no test constructs ARSessionHolder or GeoARSessionManager and none names snapNearestDropToGround, so both blockers would regress silently against a green 147/147. Neither field case is optional; a failure on either re-opens the wave regardless of every other number.
